stem: A technician sees marginal necrosis on several plants. What belongs in the initial record?
choices: Record a confirmed nutrient-toxicity diagnosis so the next shift knows what correction to make.
Recommend a new fertilizer recipe based on the visible margin damage.
Record the objective symptom location and distribution along with crop stage and available pH, EC, irrigation, and root-zone context.
Record genetics as the cause if the affected plants share a cultivar.
rationale: The initial record should capture what is actually visible and the context that may help later interpretation. Marginal necrosis can have multiple nutritional, environmental, or root-zone explanations, so Technician I should not convert the observation into a diagnosis or recipe change. A reconstructable record preserves symptom location, distribution, stage, and relevant measurements.
